page.layout: One printed page. At the top a woodcut coat of arms with a banner reading INVIVM / NIHIL VIRTVTI. Below it the title lines, centred. Below them two parallel columns of verse, left column first, then right column.

main_text.l: IN INSIGNIA
VVAMBOLDORVM AB VMBSTAT, ETC.
Epigramma
CASPARI VVASERI, TIGVRINI.
Impar Isosceleon numeris: color albus et ater,
Et Canis ad galeam cingula fulva gerens.
Hæc Vuamboldorum sunt prisca insignia gētis,
Fortibus e Franeis quæ generata viget.
Schemate Isosceleon nihil ingeniosius usquam
Architectonice ac tota Mathesis habet.
Providus est Canis atq; sagax, vigil atq; fidelis:
Sacra Magistratus munia Zona notat:
Fulvus opum: niveus pacis: Martem [illegible, ~5 letters] at-
Vuamboldis pulcrē singula conveniunt,
Artibus, ingenio, virtutibus undiq; toto
Quippe Orbe illustres, seu Cynosuris micant.
Quis vel Cesaribus dare prudens atque fidele
Consilium, vigiles Marte Togaq; queant:
Hujus eis præstant solertes munia summa:
Ina vel principibus sæpe negata viris.
Cumq; nec Eoæ desint his pondera gazæ,
Arma quibus hæc vltra tradita jure ne[?]

page.notes: The woodcut shows a shield per pale of black and white diagonal lozenges (a chequered pattern of triangles), a crest of a dog's head with a collar, and helm and mantling, with scrolls on either side. The banner above reads INVIVM, with NIHIL at left and VIRTVTI at right. The lower left of the verse is partly damaged; the word after "Martem" is unreadable. The last line of the right column is faded at its end. The page is stained and worn at the edges.
